themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Missing and dangling street signs have spiked dramatically this week in Greenpoint/Williamsburg, with 5 missing sign complaints (264% above 8-week average of 1.4/week) and 7 dangling sign complaints last week (331% above baseline of 1.6/week), suggesting accelerated infrastructure decay that poses pedestrian and traffic safety risks.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.4 weekly average (264% spike, z-score 7.49)
Street Sign - Dangling: 7 complaints last week vs 1.6 weekly average (331% spike, z-score 4.84)
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'Improve traffic and pedestrian safety' funding from DOT
reporting_angles: Document specific dangerous intersections where signs are missing/dangling; interview DOT on repair timeline
Broader story on deferred street maintenance across waterfront neighborhoods—are other CDs seeing similar spikes?

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints have surged 409% this week in CD 301, with 7 complaints vs a baseline of 1.4 per week, indicating potential disease spread, storm damage, or systematic neglect in a neighborhood with significant environmental redevelopment.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs 1.4 weekly average (409% spike, z-score 5.67)
Community Board repeatedly requests 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' from Parks Dept—trees likely part of this need
1,291 building permits filed in last 90 days (201 new buildings) suggests active construction that may stress existing tree canopy
reporting_angles: Visual walkthrough of affected blocks; interview Parks Dept on tree health assessments and removal/replanting schedule
Investigate whether construction activity (permit surge) is damaging or removing mature trees; connect to gentrification narrative

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Vendor/Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped 700% this week (5 vs 0.6 weekly average) while vendor enforcement complaints surged 627% (10 vs 1.4 weekly average), suggesting either new unlicensed activity or enforcement crackdowns in a neighborhood with active street-level commerce.
evidence: Outdoor Dining complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.41)
Vendor Enforcement complaints: 10 THIS WEEK vs 1.4 weekly average (627% spike, z-score 4.62)
Local news mentions new bar/dining scene (Hell Gate article on casual bites in Greenpoint, April 2026)
reporting_angles: Are new restaurants opening faster than city can license? Track permitting timeline for outdoor seating approvals
Interview business owners on compliance burden; speak to CB and 311 callers on what specific complaints are—sidewalk obstruction, noise, illegal vendors?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked 260% two weeks ago (9 complaints vs 2.5 weekly average), coinciding with community board's repeated requests for homeless services funding, indicating a potential concentration of street-level homelessness in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: Panhandling complaints: 9 two weeks ago vs 2.5 weekly average (260% spike, z-score 4.33)
Community Board has listed 'Other request for services for the homeless' as top-line budget request for 2+ years
Waterfront gentrification (5 active ULURPs, 1,291 permits) may be displacing unhoused populations into street-level visibility
reporting_angles: Profile encampment locations; interview Parks, NYPD, DHS on coordination and available shelter capacity in CD 301
Longer investigation: does new development (200 Kent, 20 Berry, Monitor Point rezoning) have affordable housing or social services requirements?

themes_detail.label: Sewage/Building Exterior Issues
themes_detail.summary: Indoor sewage complaints spiked 1100% three weeks ago (3 vs 0.2 weekly average) while exterior building complaints jumped 700% last week (3 vs 0.4 weekly average), suggesting potential infrastructure or building code violations in aging or rapidly-redeveloped housing stock.
evidence: Indoor Sewage complaints: 3 three weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 4.16)
Outside Building complaints: 3 last week vs 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Community Board repeatedly requests 'Other capital budget request for DEP' and 'Other expense request for DOB'—both tied to building/infrastructure issues
743 alterations filed in last 90 days; potential construction-related sewer or facade damage
reporting_angles: DOB violations audit: which buildings have repeat sewage/exterior complaints? Are there enforcement gaps?
Interview tenants in buildings with complaints; investigate whether landlords are delaying repairs while awaiting rezoning/sale opportunities
